findings: THE PUNCHLINE IS MEASURABLE AFTER ALL, and the judge said no regex would find it. Operationalised as CLOSING STING on the final sentence of a line: (b) a short (<=14w) closing sentence opening with Which/That is/And that/Nobody/No one, or (c) a trailing `, which/and that` clause or a `which is how/why/what/the` recast. Dialogue: ours 43.50 per 10k vs Morrowind 1.63 = 26.6x. Books 2.45 vs 0.05 = 45x. Journal 35.91 vs 6.06 = 5.9x. This is a bigger separator than `eleven` ever was.

AND THE HONEST HALF: the EPIGRAM-ECHO (short closing sentence repeating a content word from an earlier sentence — "That is not a mistake. A mistake happens once.") is at PARITY. Ours 27.68 per 10k vs Morrowind 23.76 = 1.16x in dialogue; books 2.12 vs 2.69 = 0.79x (they use it MORE). Morrowind writes epigrams too. What it does not do is close on a subordinate clause promoted to a recast. So the fix is NOT "stop being witty" — it is "stop appending an interpretive clause to the fact".

BIMODALITY CONFIRMED AND LOCATED, per dialogue file (words, sting/10k, q/10k, ex/10k): greetings.json 20185 / 82.2 / 49.5 / 34.7 (exclamations OVERSHOOT Morrowind's 21.25 by 1.6x); greetings/00-priority-classes.json 496 / 40.3 / 80.6 / 40.3 (1.9x overshoot); every topics/*.json file 0.0 exclamations and 0.0-8.7 questions. The seam is exactly greetings-vs-topics: the generator was swept, the topic files were not.

PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE ANY LINE WAS REWRITTEN — THE EARNED-STING RULE. An info may close on a reversal, wry qualifier or epigram only if BOTH: (a) the speaker has a personal stake the player has worked for, operationalised as the info carrying a disposition gate (`d` present); AND (b) it is the ONLY such info in its topic. Everything else closes flat: the final sentence states a fact, gives a direction, names a price, or asks the player something. This is auditable from the JSON without reading the prose — 55-utility.json has 5 d-gated infos of 102, so at most 5 of its 34 topics may keep a sting; 50-factions.json has 33 of 106 across 41 topics.

A BAR DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS IT JUDGES CANNOT SAY THE CORPUS IS WRONG. My first calibrator set caps at the 90th percentile of our own files and produced a sting ceiling of 69.65 per 10k against a reference of 2.00 — 35x the thing it measured, red on nothing. Every bar is now a fixed multiple of the measured reference (3x for caps, 0.25x for floors). Recorded because the percentile version LOOKED rigorous and was vacuous.

THE UNDERSHOOT GUARD. "This file has no exclamation marks" is evidence only when the file is long enough for the reference rate to predict some. A bar's floor half is skipped unless target*words/1e4 >= 2. Without it the check flags every 400-word file for the absence of a thing that would not be there anyway.

MY OWN CLEAN CONTROL FAILED FIRST TIME AND THAT IS THE POINT. The self-test's negative control was one flat line repeated 40 times; the line carried one exclamation mark, so at 40 copies the fixture ran at 370 exclamations per 10k and tripped the OVERSHOOT half of the band it existed to pass. A control has to be a distribution, not a sample. Replaced with 26 varied flat service lines.

THE VERDICT'S FILLER-ELEVEN LIST IS PARTLY WRONG AND I CHECKED BEFORE REWRITING. Of the six residual elevens it called uncountable, TWO are cross-referenced plot dates: "struck off the roll eleven years ago" and "Eleven years of leases" are Sedda Vell's tenure, referenced EIGHT times in game/data/quests/faction-imperial-assize.json (the signed-out fourth volume, the audit span, the office that never asked for the books back) and echoed in faction-xul-aneekh.json and magic-utility.json. Rewriting them to satisfy a tic list would have broken five files. The gate now matches only 'eleven' + a noun of DEGREE (times / kinds of / chairs of), which leaves the two genuinely indefensible ones red and lets the design motif alone — the round-1 builder had already ruled it an owner-level decision.

50-factions.json AFTER, per 10k (before -> after): sting 49.6 -> 2.9 (ref 2.0); questions 2.5 -> 55.7 (ref 159.2); exclamations 0.0 -> 11.7 (ref 21.3); contractions 25.1 -> 169.9 (ref 328.5); And/But/So 26.4 (ref 64.0); fragopen 0. All tics cleared. 79 authored rewrites.

TWO FALSE POSITIVES IN MY OWN GATE, BOTH POINTING THE SAME WRONG WAY, both caught by reading its output against the corpus. (1) countFragOpen counted "Which is it?", "Which one, citizen?" and "Which tide were you drawn on?" as the manufactured-fragment tic. (2) stingKinds counted an interrogative closing sentence as a closing sting. Both would have CHARGED A FILE FOR ASKING THE PLAYER A QUESTION — the single defect the round exists to fix — and so would have aimed the next writer at exactly the wrong target. Interrogatives are now excluded from both by the question mark. 5 of the 17 flagged greetings fragments turned out to be this.

THE POSSESSIVE CONFOUND IN THE CONTRACTION METRIC. word+apostrophe+s/t/re/ve/ll/d/m counts "Oleen's yard" as a contraction: it inflates ours from 208.0 to 244.9 per 10k and the reference from 292.3 to 328.5 — about 15% on BOTH sides, so it never moved a ratio, and round 1's 463.7-vs-327.8 greetings figure stands as a real 1.45x overshoot either way. Corrected anyway (unambiguous n't/'re/'ve/'ll/'d/'m plus 's only after a closed-class word), because the two sides are not guaranteed to stay symmetric while the proper nouns are still being written.

LEVERAGE ON THE BIGGEST FILE: greetings.json is 20,185 words (a third of the dialogue register) and its 95 sting-closing lines come from only 17 DISTINCT authored fragments in tools/dialogue/gen-greetings.mjs. Five of those 17 were my own false positive (interrogatives). The remaining 12 fragments are the whole of the file's sting defect — a bounded fix at the generator, not 95 line edits.
